recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant FHIR-3691 prose unless a future work group decision intentionally reopens contained-resource context conduction; the current no-inheritance rule is clearer and safer than the original 2015 mitigation text.
issue_request: FHIR-3691 was Published / Persuasive with Modification for a DSTU1 change request warning that informal context conduction from a containing resource into a contained resource was dangerous. The applied decision was svn revision 4615, which strengthened the references-page guidance around undefined conduction and unsafe inference.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied in git-svn revision 4615, now commit 6592747fc7f7e9122f5022a66d33b61d06aaddf4, which added warnings that FHIR provides no mechanism for defining or constraining conduction of equivalent properties into contained resources. Later commit 6bb9d508d3ed2e099a0e5909d738553572502039 for FHIR-7385 changed the same section to the stronger rule that contained resources do not inherit context.
additional_context: FHIR-5223 was an earlier Published clarification on the same ambiguous contained-resource inheritance wording. FHIR-7385 was a later Published / Not Persuasive with Modification issue that explicitly disallowed contained-resource context inheritance, and a separate FHIR-7385 reconciliation commit already on the combined branch fixed the remaining introductory contradiction. source/fhir.ini maps reference=references, so source/references.html is in current build scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source says contained resources follow the same no-inheritance rule as other references and that inline contained resources do not inherit context from their parent resource, which fully satisfies FHIR-3691's safety concern without reintroducing older out-of-band-conduction prose.
